facts.raw_span: 63-year-old man
8-month history of painless scrotal swelling
bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness
large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were all within normal limits
no evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses
7.0 × 6.0 × 4.2 cm tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types: small cells, medium cells, and large cells

concepts.why: The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis, lymphovascular invasion, and a pleomorphic tumor composed of multiple cell types are consistent with embryonal carcinoma.
The combination of a large, solid mass in the testis, lymphovascular invasion, and a tumor composed of multiple cell types could also suggest a mixed germ cell tumor.
The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis and lymphovascular invasion could be consistent with a yolk sac tumor, although the normal α-fetoprotein levels are unusual for this diagnosis.

The presence of a pleomorphic tumor composed of multiple cell types could suggest a teratoma, although the absence of specific features such as cystic components or immature elements makes this diagnosis less likely.

The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis and lymphovascular invasion could be consistent with choriocarcinoma, although the normal β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels are unusual for this diagnosis.

The presence of a large, solid mass in the testis and lymphovascular invasion could be consistent with seminoma, although the pleomorphic nature of the tumor and the presence of multiple cell types are unusual for this diagnosis.

The lack of evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on the positron emission tomography–computed tomography scan rules out lymphoma as a primary diagnosis but the test was performed to evaluate for lymphoid malignancy.

rationales.F04: Large, solid masses in both testes are more typical of testicular tumors than lymphoma.
rationales.F05: Normal serum tumor markers decrease the likelihood of choriocarcinoma and some other germ cell tumors.
rationales.F06: No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses makes lymphoma less likely.
rationales.F08: A pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types is highly suggestive of a mixed germ cell tumor or other testicular cancer, not lymphoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types and the lack of specific markers for other tumors support this diagnosis.
